result.title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions
result.comment: Accepted at the 20th International Conference on Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning (NeSy 2026). Conference version: https://openreview.net/forum?id=TEaW3pdZOZ
result.summary: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) often answer questions from incomplete records. Missing information might be interpreted as unknown or false, depending on the completeness of the source. Current evaluations fail to distinguish these two aspects, as they are usually interwoven with other reasoning demands. We present ClosureBench, a benchmark that tests whether LLMs follow the stated rules for dealing with missing information. Every base scenario is tested under OWA, CWA, and LCWA, and only the treatment of missing information changes between variants. ClosureBench provides a verified base benchmark as well as agent extensions for action choice, source scope, and updates. A model is considered correct on a base scenario only if it provides correct answers in all of its closure variants. Across 960 instances, overall accuracy can mask substantial closure mistakes. Models achieve overall accuracy from 71.18% to 99.86% across replicated runs, but their core switch accuracy, measured on the scenarios whose gold label actually changes with the contract, varies between 18.23% and 99.31%. Large discrepancies emerge under LCWA. For example, some agents choose unknown despite the prompt indicating that missing information should be treated as false. Our findings demonstrate that evaluations of AI agents should not only measure whether agents can reason over existing facts but also whether they use the appropriate assumption when information is absent.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 ClosureBench，在 OWA、CWA、LCWA 三种缺失信息处理约定下对同一基础场景做平行测试，并以「所有变体均正确」为核心判据，考察 LLM agent 是否遵循给定规则处理缺失信息。960 个实例显示总体准确率会掩盖明显的约定切换错误，部分 agent 在 LCWA 下仍输出 unknown。
AI.relevance_reason: 缺失信息应视为未知还是为假，与 LVR 中「证据是否充分、何时继续获取视觉证据或停止作答」的判断相关，其按约定变体分离度量的设计可供核查如何评价模型对信息缺失与不确定性的利用，但材料未涉及视觉或多模态状态，联系需进一步确认。
